changeReason: The first measured run showed that a syntactically valid but unknown session cookie changed public health/readiness/metrics responses from their no-cookie status to 401. R1-R7 did not require exempt public endpoints to preserve their ordinary response. Add a stricter criterion; do not weaken or replace any v1 criterion.

baselineEvidence.observed: GET/HEAD /health, /live and /ready returned 200 without a cookie but 401 with an unknown session cookie; GET/HEAD /health/metrics returned 404 without a cookie but 401 with that cookie.

criterion.source: DERIVED from the registered public health/readiness route contract
criterion.target: For GET and HEAD on /health, /health/metrics, /live and /ready, an unknown syntactically valid operator-session cookie preserves exactly the status produced without a cookie, and does not query the operator-session store.
criterion.evidence: operator-session-public-routes.test.ts and the post-fix synthetic route probe
criterion.validity: The test runs the real buildServer/Fastify hooks; store lookup count distinguishes an actual session exemption from a later coincidental status.
